dimensions.assessment: Applies to all online dating service providers operating websites or mobile applications in the United States and their entire user bases.
dimensions.evidence: An online dating service provider shall provide to a member of the online dating service a fraud ban notification

dimensions.assessment: Requires dating platforms to build automated notification workflows within 24 to 72 hours of banning a user, protecting members from financial fraud.
dimensions.evidence: provide a fraud ban notification under paragraph (1) not later than 24 hours after the fraud ban is initiated

dimensions.assessment: Enforced by the Federal Trade Commission under existing powers without creating a new standalone funding appropriation.
dimensions.evidence: The Commission shall enforce this section in the same manner, by the same means, and with the same jurisdiction

dimensions.assessment: Establishes a single national standard that preempts state laws regarding dating service fraud ban notifications and treats violations as FTC trade practice violations.
dimensions.evidence: A violation of this section or a regulation promulgated under this section shall be treated as a violation of a rule defining an unfair or deceptive act or practice

dimensions.assessment: Permanent federal mandate taking effect one year after enactment, providing nationwide coverage across all states and territories.
dimensions.evidence: This section shall take effect on the date that is 1 year after the date of the enactment of this Act.

summary: The Romance Scam Prevention Act requires online dating service providers to send a fraud ban notification to any user who has exchanged messages with an account that has been banned for suspected fraud. The law establishes standard rules for what these notifications must contain, how quickly they must be sent, and provides a legal safe harbor for companies complying with the requirement. It also sets up federal and state enforcement mechanisms through the Federal Trade Commission and state attorneys general, while establishing a single national standard that overrides state-level notification laws.

affected_groups.effect: Receive safety notifications if they have communicated with a user whose account was suspended or terminated due to suspected romance scams.
Must implement notification systems to alert users who interacted with banned accounts within specified timeframes and face enforcement actions if they fail to comply.
Granted authority to enforce the rules and bring civil actions against violators.
affected_groups.group: Federal Trade Commission and State Attorneys General

key_provisions: Online dating service providers must send a clear and conspicuous fraud ban notification to any member who received a message from a banned user.

Notifications must include specific information such as the banned user's profile identifier, warnings against sending cash or financial information, fraud avoidance tips, and customer service contact details.
Notifications must generally be delivered within 24 hours of a fraud ban, with allowances for provider judgment or law enforcement delays.
Online dating service providers receive legal protection from liability for claims brought by members or banned users based on actions taken to comply with notification requirements.
The Federal Trade Commission and state attorneys general are empowered to enforce these requirements.
Establishes a single national standard, preventing individual states from maintaining their own laws regarding fraud ban notifications on online dating services.

summary_detail.plain_summary: The Romance Scam Prevention Act requires online dating service providers to send a fraud ban notification to any user who has exchanged messages with an account that has been banned for suspected fraud. The law establishes standard rules for what these notifications must contain, how quickly they must be sent, and provides a legal safe harbor for companies complying with the requirement. It also sets up federal and state enforcement mechanisms through the Federal Trade Commission and state attorneys general, while establishing a single national standard that overrides state-level notification laws.
summary_detail.significance: The legislation introduces a uniform national requirement for online dating platforms to warn users about potentially fraudulent accounts they have contacted. It changes the operational obligations of dating service providers by imposing strict timelines and content requirements for scam warnings, while preempting state-level regulations to create a single national standard.
